sections.content: How many people are "inspectors of standards and regulations"?

15,775 people

were counted on the census as "inspectors of standards and regulations" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Inspectors of standards and regulations verify and ensure compliance with acts, regulations and other requirements in respect of: buildings, weights, measures and trade descriptions; the installation and safety of electrical, gas and water supplies and equipment; marine pollution, ships� structures, equipment and accommodation; the treatment of animals; the operation of commercial vehicles; the welfare, health and safety in factories and all work sites subject to the provisions in the Factory Acts.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "inspectors of standards and regulations" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "inspectors of standards and regulations", 16.5% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "inspectors of standards and regulations" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "inspectors of standards and regulations" included:

  • health and safety managers and officers
  • counsellors
  • managers and proprietors in forestry, fishing and related services

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "inspectors of standards and regulations" there were more men than women (62% compared with 38%).

This means "inspectors of standards and regulations" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business and public service associate professionals".

Men made up 62% and women made up 38% of "inspectors of standards and regulations"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "inspectors of standards and regulations" included:

  • protective service associate professionals (other)
  • glass and ceramics makers, decorators and finishers
  • food, drink and tobacco process operatives

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "inspectors of standards and regulations" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "inspectors of standards and regulations" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "inspectors of standards and regulations", 12.5% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (85.3% compared with 14.7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (96.4%) than self-employed (3.6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Cornwall, this is in the region of the South West.
